kill-switch.title: Internet kill switch
kill-switch.help:
When on, the internet is fail-closed. If the tunnel drops, nothing leaves this machine. Apps cannot skip the tunnel by binding a network adapter, and devices on the LAN may stop responding. Only the tunnel process and traffic already inside it can go out. Disconnecting, or turning this off, opens the network again.

Switching servers keeps the tunnel up and reloads only the outbound, so your real address does not appear in the gap. With this off, a switch is a full stop then start.

smart-connect.title: Smart connect
smart-connect.help:
When on, Connect ignores the server you last tapped. It picks the node with the lowest, most stable score from the last 5 pings — timeouts count against a node. If nothing has been measured yet, it pings the list first.

The home screen shows “Smart connect” and the best node’s country. You cannot change servers while it is on. Turn it off to connect to the server you selected. While the kill switch is on and you are connected, new pings are skipped, so the next pick uses the history it already has.

fetch-interval.title: Auto subscription
fetch-interval.help:
How often the app pulls a fresh node list from your subscription URL. It does not change which server you connect to.

Pick an interval, or Off to update only when you open the app or tap refresh on Servers.

nested.vlessHint: These fields must match the server exactly: SNI (= Reality dest), public key, short ID (empty only if the server allows it), and flow (xtls-rprx-vision when the server uses Vision).
nested.shortIdInvalid: Short ID must be hex (0-9, a-f).
nested.dnsHint: Both servers are used for proxied DNS. Local system DNS is used for direct domains.
nested.dnsFallbackHint: When the proxy is unreachable, name lookups go to whatever resolver the OS is using — usually your ISP. That is the leak this tunnel exists to prevent. Leave off unless you need the network to keep resolving without the proxy.
